topics.topic: Verdict favoring Miro for a Crit-like collaborative loop, Eraser for the architecture artifact, and tldraw for a custom interaction
topics.note: Current first-party sources retain this ordering for the stated priorities, but the verdict is conditional on hosted-board exposure and does not claim measured local-model reliability.

topics.topic: Six properties of a Crit-like diagram review loop
topics.section: The loop needs an inspectable artifact and an explicit gate
topics.note: Reframed as a review protocol: bounded inspect, durable identity, proposal, attached feedback, approval-gated mutation, and reread. The gate is a process rule rather than a documented Miro transaction.

topics.section: Current tools expose different parts of the loop
topics.note: Every retained capability was revalidated. Whimsical's current documentation establishes a fuller edit and comment surface than the source's partly verified label.

topics.section: The loop needs an inspectable artifact and an explicit gate
topics.note: The workflow now uses current canvas_search, canvas_read_as_svg, and canvas_update_from_svg names. Deprecated layout tool names are preserved only as migration history.

topics.topic: Miro comment-driven ACCEPT or REVISE protocol and reread after update
topics.section: The loop needs an inspectable artifact and an explicit gate
topics.note: Comment list, reply, and resolve operations are documented. ACCEPT or REVISE and proposal-before-write remain a proposed human-agent convention.

topics.topic: Miro OAuth, one-team connection, curated MCP surface, and daily call limits
topics.section: Miro buys review fidelity at privacy and operating cost
topics.note: Current FAQ and limits pages confirm these constraints. No AI-credit claims were needed for the decision.

topics.topic: Eraser architecture generation, editing, CRUD, export, private-file, and pricing behavior
topics.section: Current tools expose different parts of the loop
topics.note: Current pricing uses three AI diagrams rather than the source's three AI credits wording. MCP generation and CRUD remain verified; a board-comment API is not documented.

topics.topic: Figma or FigJam native-object creation and editing, seat requirements, and beta quality
topics.section: Current documentation changes the old comparison
topics.note: Remote MCP access now spans seats and plans, while modifying an existing file still requires a Full seat plus edit permission. Beta cleanup guidance remains current.

topics.topic: Lucid read and write MCP, read-only endpoint, comments, data handling, and static output
topics.section: Current tools expose different parts of the loop
topics.note: Current Lucid documentation verifies the read-only endpoint, comments, and static rather than data-linked diagram limitation.

topics.topic: Whimsical remote and desktop MCP, object editing, local open-file focus, and comments
topics.section: Current documentation changes the old comparison
topics.note: The current tool reference documents the complete comment lifecycle and a broad object edit surface. Desktop enablement still requires an open app and vendor support.

topics.topic: draw.io hosted, local MCP, and assistant-plugin paths with local-file ownership and privacy
topics.section: Miro buys review fidelity at privacy and operating cost
topics.note: The official repository now provides an explicit data-flow matrix. Local MCP and plugins keep diagram data local; end-to-end isolation also requires a local model.

topics.topic: tldraw MCP App and Agent Starter Kit as interactive and custom-review paths
topics.section: Current documentation changes the old comparison
topics.note: The MCP App supplies a quick interactive canvas in supporting hosts. A durable Crit-like review mode still depends on Starter Kit product work and production sync infrastructure.

topics.topic: IcePanel, Penpot, and Excalidraw as narrower or specialized candidates
topics.section: Current tools expose different parts of the loop
topics.note: IcePanel still lacks diagram create, draft, version, and comment operations. Penpot supports focused-page read and write but no documented comment queue. Excalidraw supports an MCP App without a documented persistent review protocol.

topics.topic: Napkin, Structurizr, and other artifact generators that do not meet the round-trip bar
topics.section: Current tools expose different parts of the loop
topics.note: Napkin remains asynchronous one-way generation. Structurizr documents AI-produced DSL followed by manual paste. No broader unsupported product claims were retained.

topics.section: Miro buys review fidelity at privacy and operating cost
topics.note: MCP separates model and board tooling, but hosted tools still process board data. draw.io provides the strongest documented local path. No local-model tool call was executed.

topics.topic: Trial order, measurement dimensions, and confidence limits
topics.section: A read-only trial can settle the choice
topics.note: The first check was narrowed to stable IDs and comment attachment on one authorized frame. Output quality, latency, cleanup effort, call count, and local-model reliability remain unverified.
